shortDescription: STRIPPED AND READY TO PUBLISH — gen 13 (icon restyle + IconTier.Emoji). Source/ is moved out to D:; do NOT restore until the user confirms the upload completed. Shared foundation for the Radius UI suite: palette, card/shape language, typography, 277 icons, world minimap bake, live map camera.
body:
## STATE (2026-08-29 18:38): STRIPPED, AWAITING UPLOAD — DO NOT RESTORE YET

`Source/` has been MOVED out of the mod folder. The tree is stripped and ready for the user to
publish via Modmixer. **Do not restore `Source/` until the user explicitly says the upload
completed** — this is the hard rule that was broken in the sixth release (see below).

- **Backup:** `D:\Rimworld\Radius UI Framework\20260829-183831\Source\` (54 `.cs` files)
- **Tag:** `source-20260829-183831`, pushed to `origin` (github.com/Astryls/Radius-UI-Framework)
- **Commit:** `76ec18a` on `main`, pushed
- **Stripped tree:** `About Assemblies LICENSE Languages Textures` + `.git .gitignore .modmixer`
- **Upload payload: 2.0 MB** (Textures 1.6M, About 285K, Assemblies 100K). `.git` is 4.7 MB and
  is skipped by the publisher.
- **DLL:** Release, md5 `f5310274c4c5dfdfa9066b114f5fcabe`, 99328 bytes, no pdb,
  `Source/obj/` was Release-only at build time.

### Restore command (ONLY after the user confirms upload)

```
cp -r "/d/Rimworld/Radius UI Framework/20260829-183831/Source" .
```

`cp -r`, never a bare `mv` — a bare `mv` EMPTIES the D:\ backup and violates protocol step 1.
After restoring, `git add` before believing any diff (autosave may have committed the stripped
tree; compare with `git diff --cached --stat <tag>`).

## Checklist status for this release

- **§1 Content freeze — GREEN.** Zero em/en dashes in About.xml, Languages, Source. 19 literal
  `.Translate()` keys used, 31 defined, **no missing keys** (the 12 extra defined are the 8
  accent names resolved by concatenation plus new refresh-label strings — a literal-only grep
  cannot see them, do not "clean" them).
- **§2 Documentation — GREEN for the first time in three releases.** `UPDATE_NOTES.txt`
  rewritten for gen 13 (also covers the refresh-label rework, which shipped in the sixth
  release undocumented). `ARCHITECTURE.md` amended: the tier table is now four tiers, the
  mermaid `Resolve` diagram includes Emoji, and a new subsection documents why tier 4 does not
  follow category. `HELICOPTER_VIEW.md` and `STEAM_DESCRIPTION.txt` still stale — see
  outstanding item 1.
- **§3 Assets — GREEN.** Preview 1280x720, ModIcon 256x256, 277 PNGs = 277 declared in
  `cs-assets.json`, zero source art.
- **§4 Metadata — GREEN.** `PublishedFileId.txt` = 3786107692 (an update), packageId
  `astryl.RadiusUI.Framework`, Harmony dependency intact (intentional load-order anchor).
- **§5 Build — GREEN.** Release, `Assemblies/` holds only `RadiusUI.Framework.dll`, no pdb.
  **Zero warnings attributable to this mod** — the `CardChrome` warning was fixed for this
  release (see below).
- **§6 Strip — GREEN.** Sweep for `.cs .csproj .sln .pdb .md .sh .py .svg .psd .log .bak .orig
  .user` returns empty.
- **§7 Performance — carried.** No new per-frame draw path since the gen-12 sign-off; the
  restyle changed pixels, not draw code. **VRAM is unchanged**: cost is dimension-driven
  (mipmaps + DXT), and the dimension histogram is identical to before the swap (233 files at
  128x128, 15 at 64x64, the rest unchanged). Disk size rose because colour PNGs compress worse
  than flat-white glyphs; that does not affect VRAM.

### The `CardChrome` warning (fixed this release)

`Type CardChrome probably needs a StaticConstructorOnStartup attribute, because it has a field
cornerTex of type Texture2D.` Present since gen 12 (`cornerTex` arrived with `MaskCorners`),
attributed to `[RimWorld]` because Verse's startup reflection scan raises it — which is exactly
why it survived a full release cycle unnoticed. Fixed by adding the attribute; no static
constructor is needed and the lazy build in `CornerTex()` is unchanged.

**Audit method that matters:** grep for static `Texture2D` **fields**, not `static.*Texture2D` —
the loose pattern matches static *methods* taking a `Texture2D` parameter and produced three
false positives. The correct check:

```
grep -rnP '^\s*(private|internal|public|protected)?\s*static\s+(readonly\s+)?Texture2D\??\s+\w+\s*[;=]' Source/
```

Only three types own such fields: `CardChrome`, `Spatial` (partial — the attribute on
`Spatial.cs` covers all parts) and `FlatScroll`. All three now carry it.

## Generation 13 — the icon restyle

Adopted the **Adaptive Work Priorities** icon language (saturated flat fill, outline in a deeper
shade of the fill's own hue, round joins). **235 of 277 files replaced.** No API break: every
path and accessor name is unchanged, the library is still 277 files, `gen_iconset.sh` and
`cs-assets.json` need nothing.

The library is now **two families plus two exclusions**:

- **135 colour emoji** — subject icons. `IconTier.Emoji`.
- **100 tintable glyphs** — control icons and anything whose tint carries meaning.
- **42 untouched** — `Anatomy/` 25, `Marker/` 8, `Chrome/` 9.

`Chrome/` was excluded by user decision: those are tiling construction parts (speech-bubble
slices, card fittings), not pictures, and restyling them risks the geometry they tile with.

**Two icons were reverted after in-game review:** `Action/Dock` (minimize) and `Action/Settings`.
The new `Dock` collapsed into three stacked bars at 16px and read as a hamburger menu; the gear
had too few, too-fat teeth and blobbed. Both restored byte-identical from
`textures-preswap-20260829-165131`. **233 of 277 now differ from the original.** General lesson:
the emoji language adds nothing to a window-chrome control that is already a pure pictogram.

### Why it is two families — the rules that decide each icon

**All colour was a dead end.** `GUI.DrawTexture(..., color)` **multiplies**. 59 call sites pass a
`Palette` colour; `Palette.InkOnAccent` is `Surface0`, near-black, so a saturated icon tinted
with it goes black. **All glyph was also wrong** — it threw away the colour that makes the style
good (user: *"some of these, like the droplet, look better as an emoji than as a glyph"*).

Two rules force tier 1 regardless of how an icon looks. Both are documented at the top of
`IconSet.Emoji.cs` and in `ARCHITECTURE.md`:

1. **ALIAS CONTAGION.** `IconSet.aliases` maps 12 retired names onto survivors; when the retired
   name lives in a tinted category the survivor inherits that constraint. `Squad/` emblems are
   read as raw `.Texture` (`IconSet.SquadEmblems[i].Texture`), which **opts out of the tier rule
   entirely**, and their consumer documents them as *"Squad glyphs (white, tinted per-squad)"* —
   colour art there cannot be protected. Forces `Common/Heart`, `Stat/Shield`,
   `Status/Burning`, `Alert/Info` to glyph. **Re-derive this mechanically from `IconSet.cs`
   rather than from memory.**
2. **CONTRAST TINTS.** `InkOnAccent` / `BandInk` / `Surface0` mean the icon sits ON a coloured
   surface and must take that surface's ink. Forces `Common/Clock`, `Occasion/Pregnancy`,
   `Event/Quest`, `Medical/Bleed`, `Action/Check` to glyph.

### `IconTier.Emoji` — the mechanism

Registered colour art resolves alpha-only, exactly like `Illustration`. The upgrade happens in
**`Reg`**, the single funnel every generated accessor and `Get()` passes through — NOT in the
generated tables. That is deliberate: it survives a `gen_iconset.sh` regeneration (the script
still emits `IconTier.Glyph` for everything, which stays correct) and it corrects `Get()`'s
prefix-inferred tier on the same path.

Only **28 of 277** icons are statically resolvable to their tint call sites; the rest flow
through helpers, parameters and lookup tables, so a *proven* safe list is impossible. The tier
makes it moot: an unaudited tint site degrades to "full colour, still dims correctly".

### Authoring recipe (reusable)

Build each glyph as an SVG `<mask>` (white = opaque, black = knockout, grey = partial alpha)
over a full-canvas white `<rect>`; that guarantees pure-white RGB with all information in alpha.
Verify with the GDI+ pixel probe: every `A==255` pixel must be `255,255,255`.

**Match the library's existing convention:** shipped glyphs are white where opaque and **black
where transparent**. Eight releases show no tint halos. Do not "fix" this.

**Minimum feature sizes on a 96px master: strokes >= 9px, gaps >= 6px.** Below that they close
up at 16px draw size.

**Tooling in `_dev/RadiusUIFramework/IconProposal/tools/`:** `montage.ps1` (composite a folder
onto a dark plate with labels), `probe.ps1` (per-PNG pixel census / tier-1 validation),
`audit.pl` (walk every `.cs`, resolve `IconSet.Get`/accessor/variable forms back to icon paths,
report which are tinted). `review.html` is the full 235-icon before/after page.

### Process lessons that actually caught bugs

**Montage the EXISTING art before authoring replacements — filenames lie about subjects.**
White-on-transparent art is invisible in every viewer, so "read the name, draw the thing"
silently produces wrong subjects. Caught: `Common/Sword` is **crossed** swords, `Common/Note` is
a **music** note, `Common/Book` is an **open** book, `Stat/Food` is a **fork and knife**,
`Alert/Info` is a **plus**. Several had already been shown and approved before the montage
caught them.

**Contact-sheet every batch — 14 of 235 failed self-review.** Two were serious:
`Action/CursorGrab` and `Slot/Gloves` both rendered as an obscene gesture (finger shapes merged
into one raised digit). Others: sword as a floating dot, flame as a droplet, pregnancy as a
donut, drought as brickwork, fist as a pouch, `Heat` identical to `Flame`.

**Two overlapping white glyphs merge into a blob.** For crossed swords (`Action/TabArmory`) draw
shape A, then a black stroked outline of shape B, then shape B — the knockout separates them.

**Verify against the manifest, not a hand-typed list.** `review.html`'s `CATS` array is parsed by
the checker, so the check cannot drift from what is rendered — this is how a missing
`Condition/EMI` surfaced. A corrupted hex (`#e8bd` + a Devanagari digit) rendered without error
and was caught only by eye.

**`git diff` lies after an autosave.** ModmixerGitAutosave (:03/:18/:33/:48) committed the swap
mid-session, so `git diff` compared against a HEAD that already contained it and reported 0
changes. Always compare against the **tag**: `git diff --name-only <tag> -- Textures`.

### Build gotchas

- **`build_mod` runs `dotnet build` = DEBUG.** It drops a pdb into `Assemblies/` and replaces the
  shipping DLL (105472 Debug vs 99328 Release). Always follow with
  `dotnet build Source/*.csproj -c Release`.
- **A Release build does NOT delete a pdb a previous Debug build left** — `DebugType=none` only
  stops it being emitted. `rm -f Assemblies/*.pdb` and `rm -rf Source/obj/Debug` explicitly.

## `_dev/` belongs at the WORKSPACE ROOT, never inside the mod folder

`_dev/RadiusUIFramework/` resolves to `<workspace>/Mods/_dev/RadiusUIFramework/` — a sibling of
the mod folders. **A `_dev/` inside the mod folder is a publish-leak of the `Source/` class.**

**`render_svg_to_png` forces this mistake**: its `outPath` is policy-guarded to the mod folder,
so art destined for `_dev/` must be rendered into a scratch dir there and copied out. This
happened — autosave committed two scratch PNGs at 15:18 on 08-29. Fixed by `git rm --cached` and
adding **`_dev/` to `.gitignore`**, so it is now structurally impossible.

## The publish protocol (user-stated, authoritative)

1. On strip: MOVE `Source/` to `D:\Rimworld\<Mod Name>\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\` AND push a backup tag.
2. The user publishes **via Modmixer** (not the in-game uploader).
3. On **"return to build mode"**: restore with `cp -r`, KEEPING the D:\ backup and the tag.
   **Only after the user confirms the upload completed.**

**HARD RULE: never restore on the assumption that publishing happened.** The sixth release
shipped `Source/` because the restore fired before the user pressed upload. 721 KB of `.cs` went
to the Workshop. It was inert (RimWorld loads assemblies only from `Assemblies/`) but nothing
surfaces it except a human reading the Workshop file list.

**Strip scope, settled by precedent:** only `Source/`. `.git/`, `.gitignore` and `.modmixer/`
stay — dotfiles the publisher skips, confirmed across eight uploads.

## What this mod is

A **library mod**. No defs, no Harmony patches. It exists so the Radius UI suite draws with one
design language instead of many forked copies of one.

Since gen 11 it adds **one `MapComponent`** (`MapCaptureDriver`), appearing in saves as
`<li Class="RadiusUI.Framework.MapCaptureDriver" />`.

**The About.xml Harmony dependency is INTENTIONAL despite zero code references** — a load-order
anchor: `Harmony -> Framework -> consumers`. Do not "fix" it away.

**This mod is edited by more than one agent session.** Always re-read from disk before editing.

## Generation history

Gen 5 shipped 08-20. Gens 6-9 shipped 08-23. Gen 10 shipped 08-25 (gene vocabulary). Gens 11-12
shipped 08-25 (`Map/` layer, rounded images). Gen 12 again 08-27 (refresh-label rework). Seventh
upload 08-27: corrective, removed a stray `Source/`. **Gen 13 (icon restyle) stripped and ready
08-29 — this will be the eighth upload.**

### Gen 11-12 essentials (unchanged)

`Map/MapCapture`: `Request` / `Cut` / `Release` / `IsLive` + `MapCaptureDriver`. **Driver
placement is load-bearing** — a capture must run after the map's `Graphics.DrawMesh` submissions
and before Unity renders; `Map.MapUpdate` ends with `MapComponentUtility.MapComponentUpdate`,
exactly that window, no Harmony. A `Window.WindowUpdate` hook does NOT work (`Root_Play.Update`
pumps the UI root BEFORE `Current.Game.UpdatePlay`). It force-submits the culled gap while
**skipping anything already inside the engine's cull rect** (a double draw re-runs every other
mod's pawn-draw postfix twice per frame).

`CardChrome.Image` / `MaskCorners`: Unity's rounded `GUI.DrawTexture` overload **silently drops
`borderRadiuses` on the ScaleAndCrop/ScaleToFit paths**, so `Image` must use `StretchToFill`.

**`MapCapture.Request` gained `refreshHz` in gen 12** — `Map/` consumers must require 12.

## Binding rules for framework edits

Additive only; never change the value behind an existing name; **rebuild every consumer after any
framework rebuild** and hash-verify their game-side copies; the 12 icon aliases are permanent;
any vanilla-overview-tab replacement uses `Panes/OverviewTab`. Prefer a new `partial` file over
editing a shared one. Always re-read a file from disk immediately before editing it.

**Consolidating duplicate art must never delete a file.** `aliases` is only consulted by
`Get(string)`; the generated typed accessors call `Reg("Cat/Name", ...)` with the raw path and
**bypass it**, so a deleted PNG makes `IconSet.Cat.Name` log "Icon missing from library" and draw
nothing. Ship identical pixels under every name instead.

**Generation rule (has cost user-facing crashes THREE times):** a consumer must require the first
generation **that cannot predate the members it uses**. World/ users assert **8**; `LabelItalic`
**9**; `Palette.Genes` / `IconSet.Gene` / `Action.Search` **10**; `Map/` and `CardChrome.Image`
**12**; `IconTier.Emoji` **13**.

Current consumer assertions: Psycasts 12, Quest Menu 12, Ideology 8, World Map 8 (item 2), Needs
Tab 5, Mission Control 3, Social Tab 4.

## Outstanding work

0. **AFTER UPLOAD: restore `Source/`** with the `cp -r` command above, then **rebuild every
   consumer** against gen 13 and hash-verify their game-side copies (binding rules). Consumers
   were tested un-rebuilt and loaded fine — the change is additive — but the rule stands.
1. **`HELICOPTER_VIEW.md` and `STEAM_DESCRIPTION.txt` still stale** (both 08-25). The
   description draft has now shipped unapplied at gens 5, 10 and 12; About.xml still carries
   gen-5-era copy and says nothing about the restyle. User's call.
2. **Radius UI - World Map under-asserts** (requires 6, uses `WorldSnapshot.BiomeColor`) -> 8.
3. **Social Tab re-point at the standard footprint** (672x756 vs 890x790).
4. **Health and Needs migrate to `Panes/OverviewTab`** (no visible change).
5. **Faction Menu carries two forks**: `Chrome/FlatField.cs`, `Source/Core/WorldSnapshot.cs`.
6. **Reconcile `gen_iconset.sh` with the `Need/` category** (4 PNGs it never emits).
7. **Re-establish the §5 md5 proof** with a clean Release rebuild after the restore.

Game-side `Mods/RadiusUIFramework` is a **junction** to the workspace: builds land in place, and
RimWorld must be closed before building or the DLL is write-locked through the junction.
